solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: First of cosmonauts in orbit so developed branch of technology

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A space mission story: something cosmonauts started in orbit grew into a whole field of technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' gives C; 'developed' rearranges C with ORBIT SO. 'In' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotics is the engineering discipline devoted to designing and building automated machines.

clue.text: Wagner opera in France's nothing unknown, I added

parts.note: rien is French for nothing
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A Wagner opera adds up to nothing in France, with an unknown extra added.
explanation.definitionFit: Rienzi is an early opera by Richard Wagner about a Roman tribune.

clue.text: Bachelor's on the verge of highway attack

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor
the roadside is the verge of a road

explanation.surface: A single man on a grass verge launches an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a forceful verbal attack, originally a volley from all a warship's guns on one side.

clue.text: Dog food? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the food word goes around the right letter

parts.note: tack is slang for food, as in hard tack

explanation.surface: A question about dog food, answered with a casual that's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, the same as to trail or pursue them.

clue.text: Well, it's a kitchen device

definitions.meaning: in fine spirits and good health, cheerful
a gadget for cutting potatoes into strips for frying

explanation.surface: A shrug of a remark: well, it's only a kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means cheerful and lively, and also names a gadget for slicing potatoes into fries.

clue.text: Thanks to Nancy, amateur discovers old kingdom

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, so thanks there is said in French: merci

explanation.surface: A grateful amateur in Nancy stumbles upon a forgotten realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' reads like a woman's name but is the French city, signalling a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was one of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of medieval England, covering the Midlands.

clue.text: Unionist has to live on new housing development

indicators.note: housing means the rearranged letters hold the Unionist letter inside
new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A Unionist politician must live on a new housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing development' reads as a building project; 'new' rearranges TO LIVE ON and 'housing' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is gradual development, as of species or ideas over time.

clue.text: Island's not half fantastic

indicators.note: not half means only one half of the word is kept, here the first

parts.note: capricious means whimsical or fanciful, fantastic in its old sense

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses that an island is fantastic, not half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like British slang for very much, but it halves the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: A small child needed about a day to find fossil

indicators.note: about means the child word wraps around the day abbreviation

parts.note: a mite is a small child
Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: A little one needs about a day to find a fossil.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammonite is a coiled shell fossil of an extinct marine mollusc.

clue.text: Abnomal self-concern, say, shown by leaderless country

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

indicators.note: leaderless means the word for the country loses its first letter

parts.note: Romania is a country in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A psychiatric note: an unhealthy self-absorption displayed by a nation with no head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abnomal' is a typo in the printed clue for 'Abnormal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive, excessive preoccupation with oneself, regarded as unhealthy.

clue.text: Jerry Maguire's principal twice gets decoration

indicators.note: twice means the assembled piece is written two times over

parts.note: a jerry is a chamber pot, informally a po

indicators.note: principal means first, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: The film hero Jerry Maguire, or his main man, is honoured twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerry Maguire' looks like the film's title character, but Jerry is a chamber pot (PO) and only M comes from Maguire.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a woolly or tufted ball used as ornament on hats and clothes.

clue.text: A state not for eating in?

definitions.meaning: takeaway food is ordered with this phrase, meaning to take out

explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a West African nation, and the two words 'to go' describe food bought as a takeaway.

clue.text: Priest from South Africa died all right

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A report that a South African clergyman passed away peacefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Zadok was the biblical high priest who anointed Solomon king.

clue.text: In favour of joining riot

parts.note: pro means in favour of
fusion is a joining together

explanation.surface: Someone backs joining a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riot' suggests disorder, but here it is the abundance of 'a riot of colour'.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot of colour is a lavish abundance, the same lavish plenty as profusion.

clue.text: One installs machinery relatively well

definitions.meaning: a tradesperson who assembles and installs mechanical parts
comparative of fit, in better health than another

explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic who sets up engines bears this job title, and the word is also the comparative of fit, meaning healthier.

clue.text: Unrewarding time without Marvin?

parts.note: Hank Marvin is the guitarist of the Shadows
less means without

explanation.surface: A spell without Marvin proves unrewarding.
explanation.walkthrough: Hank Marvin is a British guitarist, lead of the 1960s band the Shadows; the question mark marks him as one example of a Marvin.
explanation.definitionFit: A thankless job brings no gratitude or reward to whoever does it.

clue.text: Old bridge not a means of transporting eggs?

indicators.note: not means the following item is left out of the bridge word

parts.note: a viaduct is a long bridge carrying a road or railway

explanation.surface: An old bridge was not used for carrying a cargo of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'means of transporting' sounds like a road or bridge but is a body tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The oviduct is the tube through which eggs pass from the ovary in animals.

clue.text: Cushion to support back (not bottoms)

indicators.note: not bottoms means each word loses its last letter, the bottom one in a down entry

parts.note: to uphold is to support
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A cushion meant to support someone's back, though not their bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottoms' looks like what sits on a cushion; in a down clue it means the final letters, D and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To cushion furniture is to pad and cover it with stuffing, which is what upholstering does.

clue.text: Penny off fuel keeps one quiet

indicators.note: keeps means the rearranged letters hold the one word inside
off means gone bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A penny off fuel prices keeps someone happy and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' gives EFUL, the anagram of fuel, as food gone off is spoiled; 'Penny off' looks like a price cut but P simply leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful means calm and free from noise or disturbance.

clue.text: Polished and returned jade in the box

indicators.note: returned means the whole combination is read backwards
in means the horse word is placed inside the television word

parts.note: the box is slang for television, the telly or tele
a jade is a worn-out old horse, a nag

explanation.surface: Someone polished a jade ornament and put it back in its box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jade' looks like the gemstone but is an old horse; 'returned' turns T-NAG-ELE around.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished manners or style are refined and graceful, which is what elegant describes.

clue.text: Turned up at court, showing discretion

indicators.note: turned up means read upwards, backwards in a down entry

explanation.surface: Someone appeared at court and behaved with discretion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like arrived but reverses AT to TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is diplomatic sensitivity in dealing with others, a form of discretion.

clue.text: German leads with greeting for non-violent freedom fighter

parts.note: and means together with
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A German steps forward first with a friendly hello for a peaceful activist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence campaign through peaceful civil disobedience.

clue.text: Part of ship's unit's heading north-west in strong wind

indicators.note: in means these letters are put inside the wind word

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A naval unit heads north-west through a strong wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a boat's side, a structural part of the vessel.

clue.text: Female performing expected cheesy dish

parts.note: on means performing, on stage
due means expected

explanation.surface: A woman performer was expected to serve a cheesy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheesy' hints at a corny show, but the dish is literally made of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondue is a Swiss dish of melted cheese into which bread is dipped.

clue.text: Hiding strain, accountant is able to open some beer

indicators.note: hiding means the accountant letters conceal the strain word within them

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
to rack is to strain, as in racking one's brains
can means is able

explanation.surface: A stressed accountant hides the strain and manages to open a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack open a tin of beer is the informal phrase for opening a drink.

clue.text: Often nurses left parcel out

indicators.note: nurses means holds closely, so the often phrase cradles the left letter

parts.note: a lot means often

explanation.surface: Nurses often had a parcel left behind when they went out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like hospital staff but is the verb meaning to cradle.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel out is to distribute in shares, the same as to allocate or apportion.

clue.text: Passage in Purcell originally for this instrument

indicators.note: Passage in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musical passage that Purcell first wrote for a particular instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' reads as a musical phrase but signals a run of letters inside 'Purcell originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue invites the solver to name the stringed instrument the passage was written for.

clue.text: Holding socialist's firm belief

indicators.note: holding means the firm letters contain the socialist word

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a red is a socialist

explanation.surface: A socialist is gripping tightly to a firmly held belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective with 'belief' but is the noun company, CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs or guiding principles, a creed.

clue.text: Alert fellow waving flag

indicators.note: waving means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An alert man waves a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a noun for something waved but is the verb meaning to tire.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to weaken or lose energy, the same sense as to hesitate and lose strength.

clue.text: With gift of story books, extremely elated

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: extremely means the outer letters at both ends of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Given a present of storybooks, someone is overjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone possessing a natural gift or flair is gifted, which is the same as being able and skilled.

clue.text: Article seized by large river's current

indicators.note: seized by means the article is held inside the other letters

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An object is grabbed and swept away by a big river's current.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout fishing. 'Current' looks like the river's flow but means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means most recent or up to date, the newest state of affairs.

clue.text: Resort in York perhaps cancelling bill

indicators.note: cancelling means the bill letters are struck out of the longer word

parts.note: York has a well-known racecourse; perhaps marks it as one example
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A trip to a York resort, with the hotel bill written off.
explanation.walkthrough: York Racecourse is a major English horse-racing venue. 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot but means a fallback.
explanation.definitionFit: A last resort is something turned to for help, which is what recourse means.
